strengths: Novel problem formulation: Reformulating instance segmentation as RGB image generation is creative and enables leveraging powerful generative models for this task

Strong empirical results: Competitive or superior performance to SAM across multiple datasets (COCO, DRAM, iShape, PIDRay, EgoHOS), with particularly good results on fine-grained structures and specialized domains

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Well-designed study across 5+ diverse datasets with multiple baselines, proper ablation study (Table 2) validating each loss component, and extensive qualitative results
Practical significance: Reduces annotation requirements by leveraging generative pretraining; demonstrates effective transfer of learned representations to unseen categories
Clear presentation and organization: Well-motivated paper with good visual examples across domains, clear methodology description, and thorough appendices
Demonstrates effective generalization: Model trained on limited synthetic data (indoor furnishings and cars) generalizes to diverse real-world domains and objects
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is three relatively straightforward loss functions (variance, separation, mean-level); no novel architectures or training procedures; finetuning pretrained models is standard practice

Overstated zero-shot claims: Models are finetuned on specific object types (furniture, cars); calling this 'zero-shot' is misleading—more accurately 'few-category finetuning with synthetic data' rather than true zero-shot learning

Unfair experimental comparisons: Models evaluated at different resolutions (SimpleClick/DINO at 224×224 vs. SD/MAE at higher resolutions); incomplete SAM comparison (no finetuned SAM on same synthetic data); single-point prompting only
Insufficient failure analysis: Brief mention of small objects and boundary failures but no systematic investigation; missing sensitivity analysis for loss weights and prompt location
Incomplete evaluation metrics: Single-point mIoU is limiting; missing instance-level metrics (AP, boundary accuracy); no multi-prompt evaluation; no performance scaling analysis with instance count
Missing comparisons with related work: Limited baseline coverage compared to recent instance segmentation and generative model approaches; no evaluation against traditional methods for context
Computational efficiency not addressed: 29-hour training on high-end GPU mentioned but no inference time or efficiency comparison with baselines; practical deployment considerations unclear
Color space assumptions: Assigning instances via RGB colors may fail on images with specific color patterns; alternative representations not explored
Unclear practical guidelines: Paper doesn't clearly state when practitioners should use GEN2SEG over SAM; conditions favoring each approach undefined

strengths: Novel and creative approach using generative models for instance segmentation with instance coloring loss - addresses an underexplored problem
Comprehensive evaluation across five diverse datasets (COCO, DRAM, EgoHOS, iShape, PIDRay) spanning multiple visual domains (art, egocentric, X-rays, textures)
Impressive zero-shot generalization to unseen object types and image styles without category-specific mask supervision during training
Competitive empirical results - matches or exceeds SAM performance on multiple datasets despite leveraging smaller-scale pretraining
Solid technical execution with well-motivated loss functions and effective ablation study demonstrating component contribution
Strong qualitative results with compelling visual segmentations even on challenging domains
Excellent supplementary materials with detailed implementation details and extensive qualitative analysis
Clear practical significance for applications requiring domain-agnostic instance segmentation
weaknesses: Limited theoretical analysis of why generative models learn object grouping mechanisms - core claim relies more on empirical observation than investigation
Ad-hoc loss function design with multiple components featuring arbitrary choices (√|S_i| weighting, bilateral filter kernel size, normalization schemes) lacking principled justification
Incomplete comparison with foundation models, particularly SAM - more systematic and direct comparisons across all datasets would strengthen claims
Resolution inconsistency across model variants (480×640, 368×1024, 224×224) makes it difficult to isolate performance drivers and limits interpretability
Missing computational cost analysis - no runtime comparisons or inference cost evaluation despite 29-hour training mentioned
Lack of statistical significance testing with error bars or confidence intervals to validate improvements
Prompting strategy for zero-shot learning (Section 3.2) is somewhat informal and could be more principled
Training exclusively on synthetic data (Hypersim, Virtual Kitti 2) with limited object categories raises questions about real-world generalization
Limited failure case analysis - acknowledged struggles with small objects and fine boundaries deserve deeper investigation
Edge cases in loss functions (e.g., empty masks, very small objects in Eq. 2) not thoroughly addressed

strengths: Well-motivated core insight that generative models learn implicit object grouping mechanisms, with clear intuitive examples and excellent visualizations
Comprehensive evaluation across 7 diverse datasets with rigorous ablation studies systematically analyzing loss components, data diversity, model depth, and robustness
Remarkable zero-shot generalization to unseen object types and styles when trained on synthetic data only, achieving competitive results with SAM
Clear technical presentation with well-defined loss functions and reproducible experimental setup; promised code release
Practical value demonstrated by achieving strong performance without requiring 1.1B annotated masks like SAM
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: instance coloring loss is straightforward, and point-promptable segmentation uses standard techniques (Gaussian weighting, bilateral filtering); primarily application of finetuning rather than novel methods
Overclaimed zero-shot generalization: requires domain-specific finetuning for target categories and significant performance drops without it (Table 3); not truly zero-shot in practical sense
Missing computational efficiency analysis: no inference time comparisons with baselines; training requires substantial resources (4 RTX6000 Ada GPUs) without justifying computational advantages
Insufficient baseline comparisons: DINO, SimpleClick compared at different resolution (224×224 vs 480×640); primary comparison is SAM with vastly different training data (1.1B vs 86K images)
Inadequate failure case analysis: acknowledged struggles with small objects and ambiguous boundaries lack mechanistic explanation; no systematic characterization of failure modes

Reproducibility concerns: training procedure details incomplete (learning rates, schedules), data preprocessing not fully specified, multiple dataset variations with filtering criteria make reproduction challenging

Evaluation protocol limitations: COCO_exc excludes 33 classes preventing direct comparison with published results; edge detection uses custom 'weak baseline' rather than standard benchmarks; no statistical significance testing

Theoretical justification lacking: why generative models learn grouping mechanisms stated but not formally justified; connection between image synthesis and segmentation representation learning unexplored
